title: GT256 Minuteman ICBM Test Launch (Narrated)
description: Air Force Global Strike Command Airmen conducted an operational test launch of an unarmed Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile from Vandenberg Space Force Base, Calif., May 20, 2026. (Narrated)

location.text: VANDENBERG AIR FORCE BASE, CALIFORNIA, US

transcript.text: Air Force Global Strike Command Airmen conducted an operational test launch of an unarmed minute
man three intercontinental ballistic missile from Vandenberg Space Force Base May 20th to
demonstrate the readiness of the US nuclear forces and evaluate both the weapon system
and personnel who maintain it in a highly controlled testing environment.
The test launch used a randomly selected intercontinental ballistic missile pulled from
The missile was transported more than 1,300 miles and reassembled at Vandenberg Space Force
The ICBM was equipped with a single Mark 12A high-fidelity reentry vehicle and traveled
approximately 4,200 miles at a speed of more than 15,000 miles per hour to a test range
near the Kwajalenitol in the Marshall Islands.
The ICBM test and evaluation program helps ensure the current land-based leg of the nuclear
triad remains safe, reliable, and effective until its successor is fully deployed.
The 55-year-old minute man three is based in Colorado, Montana, Nebraska, North Dakota,
and Wyoming and will be replaced by the LGM-35A Sentinel.
Reporting from Vandenberg Space Force Base, I'm Airman First Class Ian Hawks.
